input.prompt: First-person view of a plague doctor standing in a small bedroom of a poor old house in a remote mountain village, present day, with the roller blinds shut and only a small bedside lamp giving weak yellow light: plain painted walls with a few damp stains and nothing hanging on them; a double bed with a dark wooden headboard, two pillows both dented, and a crumpled white sheet; a small nightstand with the lamp and a small framed photograph; on the floor next to the bed, a plastic bucket and a big bottle of bleach; a wooden wardrobe; a window with closed plastic roller blinds. One person: a young widow in her early thirties sits on the edge of the double bed facing the viewer, in a black jumper and a long black skirt, her long dark hair loose, her red, chapped hands clasped in her lap; around her neck, on a piece of string, hangs a man's gold wedding ring. She has been hiding in here for days: scared, worn out, but defiant, staring at the viewer. No hands, arms or objects belonging to the viewer are visible in the frame. Realistic photograph, evenly exposed, everything clearly readable, no dramatic shadows. 16:9, no text, no border.

Completely re-render this image in the style described below, transforming it far beyond a filter: redraw every surface, light and texture in that technique. Keep the composition: the double bed with the two dented pillows, the nightstand with the lamp and the photograph, the bucket and the bottle of bleach on the floor, the wardrobe and the window with the closed blinds, and the young widow sitting on the edge of the double bed with her hands in her lap, in the same places and poses. The one people must become drawn, deformed, grotesque characters, not photographs: strange caricatures rather than sick ones: exaggerated and distorted proportions, oversized and oddly shaped heads, eyes too big, too small or set too far apart, odd noses, long necks, big or long hands; their mouths closed, with the same tense, serious expressions as in the photo: no smiles, no grins, no visible teeth; unsettling and sinister, but healthy and well fed, with full cheeks and clean skin: never sick, wasted, dirty or dying, never cute or cartoonish. No text, no signature, no watermark.
STYLE: a 1970s European underground comic panel: bold black brush-ink outlines, expressive scratchy crosshatching, flat muted colors with no gradients (mustard, olive green, brick red, dirty beige), halftone dots in the shadows.

Remove the one people completely, with everything they hold. Reconstruct the empty room behind them naturally, in the same drawing style. Keep everything else exactly identical and in the same place: the double bed with the two dented pillows, the nightstand with the lamp and the photograph, the bucket and the bottle of bleach on the floor, the wardrobe and the window with the closed blinds, the same lighting and the same camera. Do not draw any face anywhere.

Re-render only the one people as realistic photographs: real skin with pores, real hair, real fabric and real leather, photographic lighting. Keep exactly their grotesque, deformed features from this image: the same oversized, oddly shaped heads, the same strange eyes and noses, the same closed mouths and serious expressions, the same long necks and big or long hands, with healthy skin and full cheeks, and the same proportions, silhouettes, poses, expressions, clothes and positions, pixel for pixel. Do not make them look more normal. Everything else in the image stays exactly identical.

Edit this comic drawing of an empty room. Keep exactly the same drawing style (bold black brush-ink outlines, flat muted colors with no gradients, light crosshatching only where there is shadow), the same composition and every object in exactly the same place and size. Clean only the walls and the ceiling: they become smooth, plain painted plaster in a warm off-white color, like a modest but cared-for home, with at most two or three faint damp stains. Remove all peeling and flaking paint, exposed patches, cracks, dirt streaks and texture marks that are not real objects. Do not add anything. No people, no faces, no text.

Re-render this drawing of an empty room as a realistic photograph, like an ordinary amateur snapshot, evenly exposed. The walls and the ceiling are smooth, plain painted plaster in a warm off-white color, like a modest but cared-for home, with at most two or three faint damp stains: do not copy the drawing's cracks, peeling or flaking paint, stains or hatching. Keep everything else exactly identical and in exactly the same place and size: the double bed with the two dented pillows, the nightstand with the lamp and the photograph, the bucket and the bottle of bleach on the floor, the wardrobe and the window with the closed blinds, the lighting, the camera and the framing. Do not add any people, hands or objects, and no faces anywhere.

Change the one person in this image so that they look healthy but uncanny and wrong, like the 'alternates' of analog horror (The Mandela Catalogue), or like a familiar face that is different from how you remember it: something is off, even if at first you cannot say what. The young widow: healthy and clean, not gaunt, with smooth, pale, flawless skin and long, glossy black hair; but she is wrong: her face is slightly too long and narrow; her eyes are a little too big and too far apart, very dark and unblinking; her eyebrows are too thin and too high; her small mouth is perfectly still; her neck is noticeably too long; her fingers, clasped in her lap, are too long and too thin; she sits perfectly still and perfectly straight. Push these distortions further, so that the wrongness is obvious at first glance, while they still look like real people. Keep them as realistic photographs (real skin, hair and fabric), with the same clothes, poses, positions and lighting. They must not look sick, wasted, haggard, dirty or dying: healthy weight, clean skin, normal skin color, all their teeth, eyes with irises and pupils; not zombies, not monsters, not corpses. Do not change anything else in the image.
